steps.a: This tenant has about 4.1M shipment rows. The only usable index is on `tenant_id`, so Postgres walks all of them, filters out 3.87M by status (1.4M buffer reads from disk), then top-N sorts. Smaller tenants don't notice. A composite index `(tenant_id, status, created_at DESC)` would let it read exactly 50 rows in order with no sort. It needs `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` on the primary through a migration, so I've stopped at the diagnosis; I haven't created anything.

steps.u: OK, I'll raise it with the DB owners. Thanks.

reference.summary: Diagnosed a slow tenant-scoped Postgres list query in a Go API with EXPLAIN ANALYZE. With only a single-column tenant index, a large tenant's query scanned about 4.1M rows, filtered 3.87M by status and sorted, taking about 18 seconds. Recommended a composite index on tenant, status and creation time built concurrently; ended at diagnosis with no change made.
facts: Query: SELECT ... WHERE tenant_id AND status ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT
EXPLAIN ANALYZE showed 18.3s execution, 3,871,220 rows removed by filter
Existing indexes: pkey, tenant_id, created_at only
Recommended composite index (tenant_id, status, created_at DESC) via CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
No index created; the engineer will take it to the DB owners
